brief: US tech long/short positioning (Goldman prime brokerage) is at its lowest since 2016 records began, with selling now outright short building rather than de-grossing and CTAs near maximum Nasdaq shorts, leaving room for a squeeze. Goldman separates that from a genuine leadership return: the former needs only improved sentiment, the latter needs renewed confidence in earnings and financing. Semiconductors have underperformed the S&P 500 by 30+ points since June. Goldman's AI semiconductor basket trades at 11x 2028 earnings versus nearly 16x for the S&P despite consensus 31% 2028 earnings growth, implying about a 6% earnings decline at the S&P's multiple, so either estimates collapse or the market has turned excessively pessimistic. Momentum has flipped, with AI names moving into short-term momentum's short legs while technology stays a modest 12-month buy. The bigger constraint is financing, not demand or construction capacity: AI companies want to spend more cash than they generate as borrowing costs rise. Index-weight cash flow is scarcer, and Goldman's high-versus-low free cash flow basket is outperforming. The S&P 500 ex-AI has outperformed and held up better in last week's selloff, and Europe's near-zero beta to the US AI basket makes it a diversification play.
